Print all factors of a number efficiently (up to the square root).

Supplied answer
import math
def factors(n):
    result = []
    for i in range(1, int(math.sqrt(n)) + 1):
        if n % i == 0:
            result.append(i)
            if i != n // i: # avoid repeating for perfect squares
                result.append(n // i)
    return sorted(result)
print(factors(36)) # [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36]
Note: Factors come in pairs (i, n//i), so one loop to sqrt(n) finds both.
